questions.stem: Why do lipids have a lower RQ value than carbohydrates?

options.text: Lipids produce more carbon dioxide per molecule
Lipids contain less oxygen relative to carbon and hydrogen, so need more O2 to break down
Lipids are broken down faster than carbohydrates
Lipids do not produce any carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: Lipids contain proportionally less oxygen in their molecular structure compared to carbohydrates. This means more external oxygen is needed to fully oxidise them, resulting in a lower ratio of CO2 produced to O2 consumed.
